# Istor

> Istor is a free, open research notebook for Windows that runs entirely on your own machine. Add sources, ask grounded questions, and read answers where every claim carries a citation back to the passage it came from. Retrieval, prompting and inference happen locally, so a GTX 1650 class GPU is enough hardware and nothing leaves your computer unless you trigger a web fetch yourself.

The site at [istor.fyi](https://istor.fyi/) is the product's home page. It is static, makes zero network requests at runtime, and works without JavaScript.

## Pages

- [Home](https://istor.fyi/): what Istor is, how the research loop works, hardware and privacy facts, and the full FAQ.
- [Istor and NotebookLM, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-notebooklm/): a factual comparison for people weighing a cloud notebook against one that runs on their own machine.
- [Istor and ChatGPT, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-chatgpt/): a general-purpose cloud assistant with frontier-scale models, and a local research notebook where documents never leave your machine.
- [Istor and AnythingLLM, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-anythingllm/): two open-source tools that run AI on your own documents locally, and the different bets they make.
- [Istor and GPT4All, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-gpt4all/): one built to chat on any CPU, one built to ground research answers on a modest GPU.
- [Istor and Zotero, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-zotero/): a reference manager organizes what you have read; a grounded local notebook reads it with you. Why they complement each other.
- [Istor and Mendeley, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-mendeley/): the same pairing from the Elsevier side of the reference-manager world, and what each tool's trust model means for your library.
- [Istor and Obsidian, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-obsidian/): a plain-text knowledge base of notes you write, and a local research notebook that reads the sources themselves. Two local-first tools, different jobs.
- [Can a local AI do a literature review?](https://istor.fyi/local-ai-literature-review/): what a grounded local tool contributes to reviewing literature, and where the line sits.
- [Local AI for field research](https://istor.fyi/local-ai-field-research/): the whole analysis loop offline, where ethics rules forbid uploads and coverage is unreliable.
- [Writing with sources, on a local AI](https://istor.fyi/local-ai-writing-projects/): keeping the library searchable beside the draft, with citations as you write.
- [Can you run a research AI on a GTX 1650?](https://istor.fyi/run-research-ai-gtx-1650/): what fits on entry-level GPU hardware and how the grounding loop runs on it.
- [Is local RAG private?](https://istor.fyi/is-local-rag-private/): what actually leaves the machine in a local retrieval loop, and the questions to ask of any tool.
- [What is retrieval-augmented generation?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-rag/): the technique behind chat with your documents, what it fixes, what it does not, and how it runs locally.
- [What is a local LLM?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-a-local-llm/): a language model that runs on your own hardware, what it can and cannot do, and what it takes to run one.
- [Does local AI need a GPU?](https://istor.fyi/does-local-ai-need-a-gpu/): no, small models run on a plain CPU, just slower; what a GPU buys and where research work wants even an entry-level card.
- [Can an AI do research with no internet?](https://istor.fyi/research-ai-offline/): what a local research AI does with the network unplugged, what it honestly cannot, and when offline is the point.
- [What is the most private way to chat with PDFs?](https://istor.fyi/private-pdf-chat/): a checklist for private document question answering, and how Istor satisfies each item.
- [Can a local AI read scanned PDFs?](https://istor.fyi/local-ai-scanned-pdfs/): local OCR and vision models read scans on your machine, and the limits of what photographs of pages give up.
- [What formats can a local AI read?](https://istor.fyi/what-formats-can-local-ai-read/): the common research formats read on your machine, and why a tool's format list is also its upload list.
- [Can a local AI summarize PDFs?](https://istor.fyi/can-local-ai-summarize-pdfs/): yes, on your machine; what makes a summary checkable, how long documents get handled, and where length limits bite.
- [Why do AI chatbots invent citations?](https://istor.fyi/why-ai-hallucinates-citations/): why language models generate plausible-looking references, why retrieval alone does not fix it, and what a verification gate does.
- [What is a context window?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-a-context-window/): the model's working memory, what fits inside it, and how retrieval decides what goes in.
- [What is an embedding?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-an-embedding/): the number representation that lets search match by meaning, and why the conversion runs fine locally.
- [What is quantization?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-quantization/): storing a model's numbers in fewer bits, the compression that lets serious models run on ordinary hardware.
- [What is tokenization?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-tokenization/): how text becomes the pieces a model reads, and why every limit is measured in tokens.
- [What is OCR?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-ocr/): reading text out of images of pages, where it fails, and why the conversion can stay on your machine.
- [Can a local AI translate documents?](https://istor.fyi/can-local-ai-translate-documents/): yes, translation is a core language task; what quality depends on and why the document never has to leave the disk.
- [How much RAM does a local AI need?](https://istor.fyi/how-much-ram-for-local-ai/): a quantized 7B model fits in about 5 gigabytes, so 16 GB is a comfortable setup; the model is the consumer, the library barely counts.

## Download

Windows builds live at [github.com/ThoriaDevelopment/Istor/releases/latest](https://github.com/ThoriaDevelopment/Istor/releases/latest). The source is open under the repository's license.

Thoria develops Istor. The organization is at [github.com/ThoriaDevelopment](https://github.com/ThoriaDevelopment).
